name_note: The species was formerly named Propionibacterium granulosum, and one cited study uses that earlier name.

sentences.text: Cutibacterium granulosum, formerly known as Propionibacterium granulosum, is a commensal bacterium found on human skin.
It is grouped with Cutibacterium avidum and Cutibacterium acnes as commensal skin bacteria, and is described as rarely causing infections and generally considered non-pathogenic.
Research has revealed that the multidrug-resistant plasmid pTZC1 can transfer between C. granulosum and C. acnes, the latter an opportunistic pathogen in surgical site infections.
A comparative genomic study of 30 metagenome-assembled and isolate genomes identified a pan-genome of 6,077 genes for the species.
Another study reported an extracellular nuclease, BmdE, secreted by this species that degraded Propionibacterium acnes biofilm in vitro and in vivo, suggesting competition between the two species.
